title: Reading schematic symbols
blurb: Recognize every symbol in the exam figures and explain what a schematic does and does not show.

T6C01.why: A **schematic** is a circuit diagram built from standard component symbols.
T6C01.trap: A flow chart shows steps, not electrical connections.

T6C02.why: A zigzag line is a **resistor**: current has to squeeze through the bends.
T6C02.trap: A transistor has three leads and a bar, not a zigzag.

T6C03.why: Three leads meeting a thick bar, with an arrow on the emitter, inside a circle: a **transistor**.
T6C03.trap: A lamp has no arrow and no thick bar.

T6C04.why: A small bulb dome with a filament inside is a **lamp**.
T6C04.trap: A ground symbol is a stem with hatch lines, not a dome.

T6C05.why: Alternating long and short parallel lines are the stacked plates of a **battery**.
T6C05.trap: A resistor is a zigzag and a ground is a stem with hatch lines.

T6C06.why: Two plates separated by a gap: a **capacitor**. A curved plate usually marks a polarized (electrolytic) kind.
T6C06.trap: A resistor is a zigzag, a transistor has three leads.

T6C07.why: A diode triangle with light arrows leaving it is a **light emitting diode**.
T6C07.trap: An inductor is loops, a resistor a zigzag.

T6C08.why: A zigzag with an arrow on it is a **variable resistor**: the arrow means adjustable.
T6C08.trap: Coils with an arrow would be a variable inductor; plates with an arrow, a variable capacitor.

T6C09.why: Two coils side by side with bars between them are a **transformer**.
T6C09.trap: A variable inductor is one coil with an arrow.

T6C10.why: A coil with an arrow touching it is a **variable inductor**.
T6C10.trap: Two plates with an arrow would be a variable capacitor.

T6C11.why: A flat-topped triangle on a stem is an **antenna**.
T6C11.trap: A ground symbol is a stem ending in hatch lines.

T6C12.why: A schematic shows how parts **connect**. Looks and wire lengths are left out.
T6C12.trap: Real wire length and appearance are exactly what a schematic ignores.
